This is a broad contextual association rather than a fixed biblical symbol.","primary_basis":["Deuteronomy 32:13–14 — curds from cattle and milk from the flock appear among the rich provisions God gives Israel.","Job 20:17 — streams of curds and honey represent prosperity that the wicked will not enjoy.","Job 29:6 — washing one's steps with curds depicts Job's former prosperity.","Isaiah 7:21–22 — abundant curds and honey are produced in the altered condition of the land, though the passage's implications are disputed."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Hospitality and generous welcome","basis":["Genesis 18:8 — Abraham serves curds, milk, and meat to his visitors.","Judges 5:25 — Jael gives Sisera curds in a noble or costly bowl."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A subsistence diet amid judgment, depopulation, or agricultural collapse","basis":["Isaiah 7:15, 21–22 — curds and honey may indicate survival from pastoral and uncultivated resources after cultivated land has been devastated, rather than uncomplicated luxury."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The consequences of pressure, agitation, or provocation","basis":["Proverbs 30:33 — pressing or churning milk produces curds/butter, analogously to pressing anger producing strife."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Spiritual nourishment, divine truth, or mature teaching","basis":["Some allegorical Christian readings extend the general symbolism of milk or rich food to curds/butter, but Scripture itself does not consistently establish this specific meaning for chemah."],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Chemah is variously translated “curds,” “butter,” or “thickened milk.” Christian interpretation has no settled, term-specific symbolic definition.
